subject: regcf
note: THE G2 SURFACE MAP for Reg CF: the committed corpus on the left, the de novo
encoding at jl4/examples/legal/regcf/denovo/regcf-denovo.l4 on the right.
COVERAGE IS FOUR PAIRS, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A CHOICE. The de novo
encoding parameterises six interpretation forks on an `Interpretation` record
threaded as an ordinary GIVEN (R4), and every one of its high-value decisions —
the investment limit, the issuer's 12-month cap, the financial-statement tier,
whether the exemption is available, whether ongoing reporting may cease — takes
that record as its first argument. The oracle cannot supply it.
WHY, MEASURED 2026-08-05 against this very module. The oracle's own Limits
section already says an enum-typed input field cannot be fed, because JSONDECODE
delivers a constructor name as a string. This run sharpens that: the failure is
at the IMPORT BOUNDARY, not in JSONDECODE generally. In a probe that IMPORTs
regcf-denovo, `JSONDECODE` into a LOCALLY declared enum with spaces in its
constructor names returns the constructor (`RIGHT OF \u0060the calendar year here\u0060`),
while the same decode into the IMPORTED `annual income period reading` returns a bare
string (`RIGHT OF "the calendar year"`), and the first CONSIDER over it raises
"The value \"the calendar year\" reached a CONSIDER that has no branch for it."
Imported RECORD types decode correctly, so the gap is specific to nullary
constructor resolution across a module boundary (jl4-core/src/L4/EvaluateLazy/
Machine.hs:2211-2229, the enum arm of jsonValueToWHNFTyped, with
isNullaryConstructorReturning at :2041). It bites both sides symmetrically — it is
why the identity fixture drops FormCFiling — so it is an engine limitation and not
a defect in either encoding.
TWO REMEDIES, neither taken here because both are outside P4: teach the decoder to
resolve imported nullary constructors; or add a small declared facade module beside
the deposit that IMPORTs it and re-exports each fork-bearing decision with
`the staff reading` pinned, so the map can point `sides.right.module` at the facade
and say in terms which reading is being compared. The eight pairs that would unlock
are listed under `blocked_pairs` in this note's tail.
PERTURBATION IS OFF, deliberately. The two encodings do not share a fact vocabulary
field for field: the corpus's Transfer carries `days since the securities were
issued` where the de novo carries two DATEs, and the corpus's AdvertisingNotice
carries `includes information beyond that permitted by paragraph (b)` where the de
novo carries its negation. A generator that mutates one canonical leaf at a time
cannot preserve the invariant that both sides still describe the same world — it
would desynchronise the dual representations and report the desynchronisation as a
divergence. So the battery is twenty hand-built rows that each move ONE fact and
keep every representation of it consistent, and minimality is carried by
construction rather than by the generator.
ROWS ARE UNIONS. Each row carries the union of both sides' field names. The decoder
ignores extra fields (Postel's Law, Machine.hs:2240), so each side sees only what it
declares. `rename` is used only where the two sides name the SAME fact differently —
one key, two names, consistent by construction. Where they represent the fact
DIFFERENTLY, both representations are in the row and are kept consistent by hand.
BLOCKED PAIRS, declared here so the pairing survives even though it cannot run:
issuer-eligible          left `issuer is eligible` / right `the crowdfunding exemption does not apply to the issuer` (negated) — right takes interp
issuer-excluded          left `issuer is excluded by Rule 100(b)` / right `the crowdfunding exemption does not apply to the issuer` — right takes interp
offering-within-limit    left `offering is within the offering limit` / right `100(a)(1) — the aggregate amount does not exceed the cap` — right takes interp
aggregate-offering-amount left `aggregate offering amount` / right `the amount already sold in the twelve month window` PLUS `the amount attributable to this transaction` — right takes interp
investment-limit         left `investment limit` / right `the investment limit for the investor` — right takes interp
investor-within-limit    left `investor is within the investment limit` / right `100(a)(2) — the investor's limit is not exceeded` — right takes interp
financial-statements     left `financial statements required` / right `the financial statements required` — right takes interp
reporting-may-terminate  left `ongoing reporting obligation may terminate` / right `the issuer may cease its ongoing reporting` — right takes interp
Two further corpus decisions are unpairable for reasons that are not the interp
blocker: `the transaction qualifies for the section 4(a)(6) exemption` and any pair
over `disclosure requirements are met` take a FormCFiling, whose
`the financial statements supplied` is enum-typed and hits the same decoder gap on
the LEFT; and `intermediary obligations are met` aggregates § 227.100(a)(3) with
§§ 227.301-303 over an IntermediaryArrangement, which the de novo side splits across
four separate predicates over two different records, so there is no single decision
to pair it with and pairing a part against the whole would manufacture divergence.

left.label: corpus
left.note: The committed hand-built encoding. At G2 this side is the diff oracle's reference, per SPEC.md §5.

right.label: de novo
note: The P3 deposit, unmodified. Its own TIMEZONE declaration is America/New_York, taken
on the EDGAR convention and registered as fork A-TIMEZONE — the two sides agreeing
on the zone here is a coincidence of convention, not evidence about the source.

rename.to a member of the family of the purchas: to a member of the family of the purchaser or the equivalent, to a trust controlled by the purchaser, to a trust created for the benefit of such a family member, or in connection with the death or divorce of the purchaser or other similar circumstance

right.note: The de novo Transfer carries two DATEs where the corpus carries `days since the securities were issued`; both are in every row and are kept arithmetically consistent by hand. The family limb is the same fact under two slightly different wordings, so it is renamed rather than duplicated.

The de novo Communication serves §§ 227.204(b), 227.205 and 227.206(b) at once, so it has ten fields where the corpus's AdvertisingNotice has five. `includes no more than the information specified in § 227.204(b)(1) through (3)` is the negation of the corpus's `includes information beyond that permitted by paragraph (b)`; a rename cannot invert a boolean, so both keys are in every row and are kept opposite by hand.

Same type name, different content. The corpus takes accreditation as one boolean input (`an accredited investor as defined in Rule 501`); the de novo COMPUTES it from § 230.501(a)(5)-(6), including the primary-residence arithmetic. Every row therefore sets the corpus's boolean to what the de novo side should compute, and a divergence on this pair is a claim about the arithmetic, not about the pairing.

perturbation.note: Off by construction; see the map note. The seed rows are already one-fact-apart from each other, so a divergence row names its own minimal witness.

note: Twenty hand-built rows. The subject sidecar's p7-dmn cases file is NOT used: its
context is in the corpus's field vocabulary, and the de novo records declare many
fields it does not supply, which the decoder reports as `Missing required field`
rather than defaulting. Rows are written in the corpus's vocabulary where both
sides have a corresponding field, per the schema, and carry the de novo side's
extra fields under their own names.

pairs.note: The one place the two encodings' date models meet head-on: a day count against date arithmetic. Row `the 365th day of a leap-spanning holding` is built to find the difference if there is one.

pairs.note: Asymmetric by design: the corpus asks for accreditation as a fact, the de novo derives it. The eight income/net-worth boundary rows are where that difference either shows up or does not.
